name: Flight Instructor Instrument (CFII)
about: Ground school for the instrument instructor rating (airplane), built from the CFII Practical Test Standards, FAA-S-8081-9E, with references at their current editions. Area I, Fundamentals of Instructing, is its own course. The multiengine Tasks IX.C and IX.D are not included.

see_also.title: Fundamentals of Instructing
see_also.note: Not tested when you already hold a flight instructor certificate; tested when the CFII is your first instructor rating.

tasks.title: Aircraft Flight Instruments and Navigation Equipment
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge of aircraft:
notes: The evaluator shall select TASKS A and D and at least one other TASK.

knowledge.text: Flight instrument systems and their operating characteristics to include:
Pitot-static system.
Attitude indicator.
Heading indicator/horizontal situation indicator/radio magnetic indicator.
Magnetic compass.
Turn-and-slip indicator/turn coordinator.
Electrical system.
Vacuum system.
Electronic engine instrument display.
Primary flight display, if installed.
Navigation equipment and their operating characteristics to include:
VHF omnirange (VOR).
DME.
ILS.
Marker beacon receiver/indicators.
ADF.
Transponder/altitude encoding.
Electronic flight instrument display.
GPS.
Automatic pilot.
FMS.
Multifunction display, if installed.
Anti-ice/deicing and weather detection equipment and their operating characteristics to include:
Airframe.
Propeller or rotor.
Air intake.
Fuel system.
Pitot-static system.
Radar/lightning detection system.
Other inflight weather systems.

tasks.title: Aeromedical Factors
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge of the elements related to aeromedical factors by describing the effects, corrective action, and safety considerations of:
notes: The evaluator shall select TASKS A and D and at least one other TASK.

knowledge.text: Hypoxia.
Hyperventilation.
Middle ear and sinus problems.
Spatial disorientation.
Motion sickness.
Alcohol and drugs.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Evolved gases from scuba diving.
Stress and fatigue.

tasks.title: Regulations and Publications Related to IFR Operations
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge of the elements related to regulations and publications, (related to instrument flight and instrument flight instruction) their purpose, general content, availability, and method of revision by describing:
notes: The evaluator shall select TASKS A and D and at least one other TASK.

knowledge.text: FAA-H-8083-15, Instrument Flying Handbook.
Aeronautical Information Manual.
Practical Test Standards.
Chart Supplement.
Standard Instrument Departures/Terminal Arrivals.
En Route Charts.
Standard Instrument Approach Procedure Charts.

tasks.title: Logbook Entries Related to Instrument Instruction
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge of logbook entries related to instrument instruction by describing:
notes: The evaluator shall select TASKS A and D and at least one other TASK.

knowledge.text: Logbook entries or training records for instrument flight/instrument flight instruction or ground instruction given.
Preparation of a recommendation for an instrument rating practical test, including appropriate logbook entry.
Required endorsement of a pilot logbook for satisfactory completion of an instrument proficiency check.
Required flight instructor records.

tasks.title: Weather Information
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge related to IFR weather information.
notes: The evaluator shall select at least one TASK.

If the current weather reports, forecasts, or other pertinent information is not available, or if the current weather is not appropriate for the practical test scenario, then weather reports, forecasts, and other pertinent information shall be simulated by the evaluator in a manner to adequately measure the applicant's competence.

knowledge.text: Sources of weather:
AWOS, ASOS, and ATIS reports.
Sources of weather data (e.g., National Weather Service, Flight Service) for flight planning purposes.
Weather reports and charts:
METAR, TAF, and Graphical Forecasts for Aviation (GFA).
Inflight weather advisories.
Surface analysis, weather depiction, and radar summary charts.
Significant weather prognostic charts.
Winds and temperatures aloft charts.
PIREPS.
Freezing level charts.
Severe weather outlook charts.
SIGMETs and AIRMETs.

tasks.title: Cross-Country Flight Planning
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge of cross-country flight planning by describing the:
notes: The evaluator shall select at least one TASK.

knowledge.text: Regulatory requirements for instrument flight within various types of airspace.
Computation of estimated time en route and total fuel requirement for an IFR cross-country flight.
Selection and correct interpretation of the current and applicable en route charts, RNAV, DPs, STARs, and standard IAP.
Procurement and interpretation of the applicable NOTAM information.
Completes and files an IFR flight plan that accurately reflects the conditions of the proposed flight. (Does not have to be filed with ATC.).
Demonstrates adequate knowledge of GPS and RAIM capability, when aircraft is so equipped.
Demonstrates the ability to recognize wing contamination due to airframe icing.
Demonstrates adequate knowledge of the adverse effects of airframe icing during landing phases of flight and corrective actions: pretakeoff, takeoff, and cruise.
Demonstrates familiarity with any icing procedures and/or information published by the manufacturer that is specific to the aircraft used on the practical test.

tasks.title: Instrument Flight Deck Check
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge of an instrument flight deck check by describing the reasons for the check and the detection of defects that could affect safe instrument flight. The check shall include:
notes: The evaluator shall select at least one TASK.

knowledge.text: Communications equipment.
Navigation equipment.
Magnetic compass.
Heading indicator/horizontal situation indicator/remote magnetic indicator.
Attitude indicator.
Altimeter.
Turn-and-slip indicator/turn coordinator.
Vertical-speed indicator.
Airspeed indicator.
Outside air temperature.
Clock.
Pitot heat.
Electronic flight instrument display.
Traffic awareness/warning/avoidance system.
Terrain awareness/warning/alert system.
FMS.
Automatic pilot.

areas.title: Preflight Lesson on a Maneuver to be Performed in Flight

tasks.title: Maneuver Lesson
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge of the selected maneuver by:
notes: The evaluator shall select at least one maneuver from AREAS OF OPERATION VI through IX and ask the applicant to present a preflight lesson on the selected maneuver as the lesson would be taught to a student. Previously developed lesson plans from the applicant's library may be used.

knowledge.text: Using a lesson plan that includes all essential items to make an effective and organized presentation.
Stating the objective.
Giving an accurate, comprehensive oral description of the maneuver, including the elements and associated common errors.
Using instructional aids, as appropriate.
Describing the recognition, analysis, and correction of common errors.

areas.title: Air Traffic Control Clearances and Procedures

tasks.title: Air Traffic Control Clearances
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge of air traffic control clearances by describing:
notes: The evaluator shall select at least one TASK.

knowledge.text: Pilot and controller responsibilities to include tower, en route control, and clearance void times.
Correct and timely copying of an ATC clearance.
Ability to comply with the clearance.
Correct and timely read-back of an ATC clearance, using standard phraseology.
Correct interpretation of an ATC clearance and, when necessary, request for clarification, verification, or change.
Setting of communication and navigation frequencies in compliance with an ATC clearance.

tasks.title: Compliance with Departure, En Route, and Arrival Procedures and Clearances
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge of the elements related to compliance with departure, en route, and arrival procedures and clearances by describing:
notes: The evaluator shall select at least one TASK.

knowledge.text: Selection and use of current and appropriate navigation publications.
Pilot and controller responsibilities with regard to DPs, En Route Low and High Altitude Charts, and STARs.
Selection and use of appropriate communications frequencies.
Selection and identification of the navigation aids.
Accomplishment of the appropriate checklist items.
Pilot's responsibility for compliance with vectors and also altitude, airspeed, climb, descent, and airspace restrictions.
Pilot's responsibility for the interception of courses, radials, and bearings appropriate to the procedure, route, or clearance.
Procedures to be used in the event of two-way communications failure.

The uses of the multifunction display and other graphical navigational displays, if installed, to monitor position track, wind drift, and other parameters to maintain situational awareness and desired flightpath.

tasks.title: Straight-and-Level Flight
notes: The evaluator shall select TASK H and at least one other TASK. The applicant shall select either the primary and supporting or the control and performance method for teaching this AREA OF OPERATION.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of teaching straight-and-level flight by describing:
The relationship of pitch, bank, and power in straight-and-level flight.
Procedure using full panel and partial panel.
Coordination of controls and trim.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to straight-and-level flight by describing:
Slow or improper cross-check during straight-and-level flight.
Improper power control.
Failure to make smooth, precise corrections, as required.
Uncoordinated use of controls.
Improper trim control.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains straight-and-level flight from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to straight-and-level flight.

tasks.title: Turns
notes: The evaluator shall select TASK H and at least one other TASK. The applicant shall select either the primary and supporting or the control and performance method for teaching this AREA OF OPERATION.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of teaching turns by describing:
The relationship of true airspeed and angle of bank to a standard rate turn.
Technique and procedure using full panel and partial panel for entry and recovery of a constant rate turn, including the performance of a half-standard rate turn.
Coordination of controls and trim.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to turns by describing:
Improper cross-check procedures.
Improper bank control during roll-in and roll-out.
Failure to make smooth, precise corrections, as required.
Uncoordinated use of controls.
Improper trim technique.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains turns from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to turns.

tasks.title: Change of Airspeed in Straight-and-Level and Turning Flight
notes: The evaluator shall select TASK H and at least one other TASK. The applicant shall select either the primary and supporting or the control and performance method for teaching this AREA OF OPERATION.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of teaching change of airspeed in straight-and-level flight and turns by describing:
Procedure using full panel and partial panel for maintaining altitude and changing airspeed in straight-and-level and turning flight.
Coordination of controls and trim technique.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to changes of airspeed in straight-and-level and turning flight by describing:
Slow or improper cross-check during straight-and-level flight and turns.
Improper power control.
Failure to make smooth, precise corrections, as required.
Uncoordinated use of controls.
Improper trim technique.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains changes of airspeed in straight-and-level and turning flight from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to changes of airspeed in straight-and-level and turning flight.

tasks.title: Constant Airspeed Climbs and Descents
notes: The evaluator shall select TASK H and at least one other TASK. The applicant shall select either the primary and supporting or the control and performance method for teaching this AREA OF OPERATION.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of constant airspeed climbs and descents by describing:
Procedure using full panel and partial panel for an entry into a straight climb or climbing turn, from either cruising or climbing airspeed.
A stabilized straight climb or climbing turn.
A level-off from a straight climb or climbing turn, at either cruising or climbing airspeed.
Procedure using full panel and partial panel for an entry into a straight descent or descending turn from either cruising or descending airspeed.
A stabilized straight descent or descending turn.
A level-off from a straight descent or descending turn, at either cruising or descending airspeed.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to constant airspeed climbs and descents by describing:
Failure to use a proper power setting and pitch attitude.
Improper correction of vertical rate, airspeed, heading, or rate-of-turn errors.
Uncoordinated use of controls.
Improper trim control.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains a constant airspeed climb and a constant airspeed descent from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to constant airspeed climbs and descents.

tasks.title: Constant Rate Climbs and Descents
notes: The evaluator shall select TASK H and at least one other TASK. The applicant shall select either the primary and supporting or the control and performance method for teaching this AREA OF OPERATION.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of constant rate climbs and descents by describing:
Procedure using full panel and partial panel for an entry into a constant rate climb or descent.
A stabilized constant rate straight climb or climbing turn, using the vertical speed indicator.
A level-off from a constant rate straight climb or climbing turn.
An entry into a constant rate straight descent or descending turn.
A stabilized constant rate straight descent or descending turn using the vertical speed indicator.
Level-off from a constant rate straight descent or descending turn.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to constant rate climbs and descents by describing:
Failure to use a proper power setting and pitch attitude.
Improper correction of vertical rate, airspeed, heading, or rate-of-turn errors.
Uncoordinated use of controls.
Improper trim control.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains a constant rate climb and a constant rate descent from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to constant rate climbs and descents.

tasks.title: Timed Turns to Magnetic Compass Headings
notes: The evaluator shall select TASK H and at least one other TASK. The applicant shall select either the primary and supporting or the control and performance method for teaching this AREA OF OPERATION.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of timed turns to magnetic compass headings by describing:
Operating characteristics and errors of the magnetic compass.
Calibration of the miniature aircraft of the turn coordinator 1, both right and left, using full panel and the clock.
Procedures using full panel and partial panel performing compass turns to a specified heading.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to timed turns to magnetic compass headings by describing:
Incorrect calibration procedures.
Improper timing.
Uncoordinated use of controls.
Improper trim control.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains timed turns to magnetic compass headings from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to timed turns to magnetic compass headings.

tasks.title: Steep Turns
notes: The evaluator shall select TASK H and at least one other TASK. The applicant shall select either the primary and supporting or the control and performance method for teaching this AREA OF OPERATION.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of steep turns by describing:
Procedure using full panel and partial panel for entry and recovery of a steep turn.
The need for a proper instrument cross-check.
Roll-in/roll-out procedure.
Coordination of control and trim.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to steep turns by describing:
Failure to recognize and make proper corrections for pitch, bank, or power errors.
Failure to compensate for precession of the horizon bar of the attitude indicator.
Uncoordinated use of controls.
Improper trim technique.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains steep turns from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to steep turns.

tasks.title: Recovery from Unusual Flight Attitudes
notes: The evaluator shall select TASK H and at least one other TASK. The applicant shall select either the primary and supporting or the control and performance method for teaching this AREA OF OPERATION.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of recovery from unusual flight attitudes by describing:
Conditions or situations which contribute to the development of unusual flight attitudes.
Procedure using full panel and partial panel for recovery from nose-high and nose-low unusual flight attitudes.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to recovery from unusual flight attitudes by describing:
Incorrect interpretation of the flight instruments.
Inappropriate application of controls.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains recovery from unusual flight attitudes, solely by reference to instruments, from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to recovery from unusual flight attitudes.

tasks.title: Intercepting and Tracking Navigational Systems and DME Arcs
tasks.references: 14 CFR part 91; FAA-H-8083-9B; FAA-H-8083-15B; FAA-S-ACS-8C; AIM
notes: The evaluator shall select TASK A and B. If aircraft is not DME equipped, performance of DME arcs shall be tested orally.
While the applicant is expected to be able to fly DME arcs, they may be selected for testing only if they are charted and available (including use of RNAV substitution techniques, if appropriate.).

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of the elements of intercepting and tracking navigational systems and DME arcs by describing:
Tuning and identification of a navigational facility.
Setting of a selected course on the navigation selector or the correct identification of a selected bearing on the RMI.
Method for determining aircraft position relative to a facility.
Procedure for intercepting and maintaining a selected course.
Procedure for intercepting and maintaining a DME arc.
Procedure for intercepting a course or localizer from a DME arc.
Recognition of navigation facility or waypoint passage.
Recognition of navigation receiver or facility failure.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to intercepting and tracking navigational systems and DME arcs by describing:
Incorrect tuning and identification procedures.
Failure to properly set the navigation selector on the course to be intercepted.
Failure to use proper procedures for course or DME arc interception and tracking.
Improper procedures for intercepting a course or localizer from a DME arc.
Exhibits instructional knowledge on the uses of the MFD and other graphical navigational displays, if installed, to monitor position in relation to the desired flightpath during holding.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains intercepting and tracking navigational systems and DME arcs from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to intercepting and tracking navigational systems and DME arcs.

tasks.title: Holding Procedures
tasks.references: 14 CFR part 91; FAA-H-8083-9B; FAA-H-8083-15B; FAA-S-ACS-8C; AIM
notes: The evaluator shall select TASK A and B. If aircraft is not DME equipped, performance of DME arcs shall be tested orally.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of holding procedures by describing:
Setting of aircraft navigation equipment.
Requirement for establishing the appropriate holding airspeed for the aircraft and altitude.
Recognition of arrival at the holding fix and the prompt initiation of entry into the holding pattern.
Timing procedure.
Correction for wind drift.
Use of DME in a holding pattern.
Compliance with ATC reporting requirements.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to holding procedures by describing:
Incorrect setting of aircraft navigation equipment.
Inappropriate altitude, airspeed, and bank control.
Improper timing.
Improper wind drift correction.
Failure to recognize holding fix passage.
Failure to comply with ATC instructions.
Exhibits instructional knowledge on the use of the MFD and other graphical navigational displays, if installed, to monitor position in relation to the desired flightpath during holding.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains holding procedures from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to holding procedures.

tasks.title: Nonprecision Instrument Approach (NPA)
tasks.references: 14 CFR part 91; FAA-H-8083-9B; FAA-H-8083-15B; FAA-S-ACS-8C; IAP; AIM
notes: The evaluator shall select TASKS A and B, to be combined with TASK C, D, or E. At least one nonprecision approach procedure shall be accomplished without the use of the gyroscopic heading and attitude indicators under simulated instrument conditions. Circling approaches are not applicable to helicopters.
The evaluator has discretion to have the applicant perform a landing or a missed approach at the completion of each approach.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of the elements of a nonprecision instrument approach by describing:
Selection of the appropriate instrument approach procedure chart.
Pertinent information on the selected instrument approach chart.
Radio communications with ATC and compliance with ATC clearances, instructions, and procedures.
Appropriate aircraft configuration, airspeed, and checklist items.
Selection, tuning, identification, and determination of operational status of ground and aircraft navigation equipment.
Adjustments applied to the published MDA and visibility criteria for the aircraft approach category.
Maintenance of altitude, airspeed, and track, where applicable.
Establishment and maintenance of an appropriate rate of descent during the final approach segment.

Factors that should be considered in determining whether: (1) the approach should be continued straight-in to a landing; (2) a circling approach to a landing should be made; or (3) a missed approach should be performed.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to a nonprecision instrument approach by describing:
Failure to have essential knowledge of the information on the instrument approach chart.
Incorrect communications procedures or noncompliance with ATC clearances or instructions.
Failure to accomplish checklist items.
Faulty basic instrument flying technique.
Inappropriate descent below the MDA.

Exhibits instructional knowledge on the uses of the MFD and other graphical navigational displays, if installed, to monitor position, track, wind drift, and other parameters to maintain desired flightpath.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains a nonprecision instrument approach from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to a nonprecision instrument approach.

tasks.title: Precision Instrument Approach (PA)
tasks.references: 14 CFR part 91; FAA-H-8083-9B; FAA-H-8083-15B; FAA-S-ACS-8C; IAP; AIM
notes: The evaluator shall select TASKS A and B, to be combined with TASK C, D, or E. At least one nonprecision approach procedure shall be accomplished without the use of the gyroscopic heading and attitude indicators under simulated instrument conditions. Circling approaches are not applicable to helicopters.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of a precision instrument approach by describing:
Selection of the appropriate instrument approach chart.
Pertinent information on the selected instrument approach chart.
Selection, tuning, identification, and determination of operational status of ground and aircraft navigation equipment.
Radio communications with ATC and compliance with ATC clearances, instructions, and procedures.
Appropriate aircraft configuration, airspeed, and checklist items.
Adjustments applied to the published DH/DA and visibility criteria for the aircraft approach category.
Maintenance of altitude, airspeed, and track, where applicable.
Establishment and maintenance of an appropriate rate of descent during the final approach segment.

Factors that should be considered in determining whether: (1) the approach should be continued straight-in to a landing; (2) a circling approach to a landing should be made; or (3) a missed approach should be performed.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to a precision instrument approach by describing:
Failure to have essential knowledge of the information on the instrument approach procedure chart.
Incorrect communications procedures or noncompliance with ATC clearances.
Failure to accomplish checklist items.
Faulty basic instrument flying technique.
Inappropriate application of DH/DA.
Exhibits instructional knowledge on the uses of the MFD and other parameters to maintain desired flightpath.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains a precision instrument approach from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to a precision instrument approach.

tasks.title: Missed Approach
tasks.references: 14 CFR part 91; FAA-H-8083-9B; FAA-H-8083-15B; FAA-S-ACS-8C; IAP; AIM
notes: The evaluator shall select TASKS A and B, to be combined with TASK C, D, or E. At least one nonprecision approach procedure shall be accomplished without the use of the gyroscopic heading and attitude indicators under simulated instrument conditions. Circling approaches are not applicable to helicopters.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of a missed approach procedure by describing:
Pertinent information on the selected instrument approach chart.
Conditions requiring a missed approach.
Initiation of the missed approach, including the prompt application of power, establishment of a climb attitude, and reduction of drag.
Required report to ATC.
Compliance with the published or alternate missed approach procedure.
Notification of ATC if the aircraft is unable to comply with a clearance, instruction, restriction, or climb gradient.
Performance of recommended checklist items appropriate to the go-around procedure.
Importance of positive aircraft control.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to a missed approach by describing:
Failure to have essential knowledge of the information on the instrument approach chart.
Failure to recognize conditions requiring a missed approach.
Failure to promptly initiate a missed approach.
Failure to make the required report to ATC.
Failure to comply with the missed approach procedure.
Faulty basic instrument flying technique.
Descent below the MDA prior to initiating a missed approach.
Exhibits instructional knowledge on the uses of the MFD and other graphical navigational displays, if installed, to monitor position and track to help navigate the missed approach.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains a missed approach from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to a missed approach.

tasks.title: Circling Approach (Airplane)
tasks.references: 14 CFR part 91; FAA-H-8083-9B; FAA-H-8083-15B; FAA-S-ACS-8C; IAP; AIM
notes: The evaluator shall select TASKS A and B, to be combined with TASK C, D, or E. At least one nonprecision approach procedure shall be accomplished without the use of the gyroscopic heading and attitude indicators under simulated instrument conditions. Circling approaches are not applicable to helicopters.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of the elements of a circling approach by describing:
Selection of the appropriate circling approach maneuver considering the maneuvering capabilities of the aircraft.
Circling approach minimums on the selected instrument approach chart.
Compliance with advisories, clearance instructions, and/or restrictions.
Importance of flying a circling approach pattern that does not exceed the published visibility criteria.
Maintenance of an altitude no lower than the circling MDA until in a position from which a descent to a normal landing can be made.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to a circling approach by describing:
Failure to have essential knowledge of the circling approach information on the instrument approach chart.
Failure to adhere to the published MDA and visibility criteria during the circling approach maneuver.
Inappropriate pilot technique during transition from the circling maneuver to the landing approach.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains a circling approach from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to a circling approach.

tasks.title: Landing from a Straight-in Approach
tasks.references: 14 CFR part 91; FAA-H-8083-9B; FAA-H-8083-15B; FAA-S-ACS-8C; IAP; AIM
notes: The evaluator shall select TASKS A and B, to be combined with TASK C, D, or E. At least one nonprecision approach procedure shall be accomplished without the use of the gyroscopic heading and attitude indicators under simulated instrument conditions. Circling approaches are not applicable to helicopters.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of the elements related to landing from a straight-in approach by describing:
Effect of specific environmental, operational, and meteorological factors.
Transition to, and maintenance of, a visual flight condition.
Adherence to ATC advisories, such as NOTAMs, wind shear, wake turbulence, runway surface, and braking conditions.
Completion of appropriate checklist items.
Maintenance of positive aircraft control.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to landing from a straight-in approach by describing:
Inappropriate division of attention during the transition from instrument to visual flight conditions.
Failure to complete required checklist items.
Failure to properly plan and perform the turn to final approach.
Improper technique for wind shear, wake turbulence, and crosswind.
Failure to maintain positive aircraft control throughout the complete landing maneuver.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains a landing from a straight-in approach from an instructional standpoint.
Analyzes and corrects simulated common errors related to landing from a straight-in approach.

tasks.title: Loss of Communications
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge of the elements related to loss of communications by describing:
tasks.references: 14 CFR part 91; FAA-H-8083-9B; FAA-H-8083-15B; FAA-S-ACS-8C; IAP; AIM
notes: The evaluator shall select at least one TASK. The evaluator shall omit TASKS C and D unless the applicant furnishes a multiengine airplane for the practical test, then TASK C or D is mandatory.

knowledge.text: Recognition of loss of communications.
When to continue with flight plan as filed or when to deviate.
How to determine the time to begin an approach at destination.

tasks.title: Approach with Loss of Primary Flight Instrument Indicators
tasks.references: 14 CFR part 91; FAA-H-8083-9B; FAA-H-8083-15B; FAA-S-ACS-8C; IAP; AIM
notes: The evaluator shall select at least one TASK. The evaluator shall omit TASKS C and D unless the applicant furnishes a multiengine airplane for the practical test, then TASK C or D is mandatory.

knowledge.text: Exhibits instructional knowledge of the elements related to loss of primary flight instrument indicators by describing:
Recognition of inaccurate or inoperative primary instrument indicators and advising ATC and the evaluator.
Notification of ATC or evaluator anytime that the aircraft is unable to comply with an ATC clearance or whether able to continue the flight.
Importance of utilizing navigation equipment in an emergency situation and demonstrating a nonprecision approach without the use of primary flight instruments.
Exhibits instructional knowledge of common errors related to loss of primary flight instrument indicators by describing:
Recognition of failed system components that relate to primary flight instrument indication(s).
Failure to notify ATC of situation.
Failure to transition to emergency mode/standby instrumentation.

skills.text: Demonstrates and simultaneously explains loss of primary flight instrument indicators by conducting a non-precision approach without the use of these indicators.
Analyzes and corrects common errors related to loss of primary flight instrument indicators.

tasks.title: Checking Instruments and Equipment
tasks.objective: To determine that the applicant exhibits instructional knowledge of the elements related to checking instruments and equipment by describing:

knowledge.text: Importance of noting instruments and navigation equipment for improper operation.
Reasons for making a written record of improper operation or failure and/or calibration of instruments prior to next IFR flight.
